scenes.title: Run a brain experiment before you book the scanner

items.text: StillHere: a researcher types a study, Meta's models build and check the stimuli, TRIBE v2 forecasts the brain response, and real public scans show how far to trust it.
Research tool for brain-imaging labs. Healthy volunteers and public data. Not a diagnosis or medical advice.
If I remove the faces from this film scene, what changes in the brain?

scenes.title: Muse Spark plans it, with a control

items.text: Muse Spark turned the question into a study: the intact film, a version with the faces removed, and an equal-area control with the same amount of picture removed somewhere else.

rows: Tears of Steel, film time 10-180 s
{N} real viewers of the intact film (Emo-FilM)

items.text: Swap for the planner's real card once the film is in the validation table.
SAM 3.1 masked every face in three minutes of film; StillHere removed them, and removed the same area elsewhere for the control.

scenes.title: Edit check: Spark Open and Glimmer

pass.text: Edit check: Spark Open and Glimmer saw a face in {k_int} of {N} intact frames, none in {k_rem} of {N} edited ones, and still saw faces in {k_am} of {N} control frames.

fail.text: Edit check failed ({detail}), so the face-map test did not run.

common.left: TRIBE: where removing faces changes the forecast
common.right: {N} real viewers: where the brain tracked faces

PASS.text: SAM masked the faces; TRIBE forecast the change; that forecast lined up with where {N} real viewers' brains tracked faces in the intact film ({k} of {N} viewers, p = {p}), and more than for the equal-area control.

PASS_visual.text: SAM masked the faces; TRIBE forecast the change; that forecast lined up with where {N} real viewers' brains tracked faces in the intact film ({k} of {N} viewers, p = {p}), and more than for the equal-area control. Most of the match comes from visual-network areas.

FAIL_not_face_specific.text: TRIBE's forecast lined up with where {N} real viewers' brains tracked faces ({k} of {N}), but no better than its forecast for the equal-area control: not face-specific.

FAIL.text: TRIBE's forecast of the face edit did not line up with where {N} real viewers' brains tracked faces ({k} of {N} viewers, p = {p}). We show it because we said we would.

UNINFORMATIVE.text: The {N} viewers' own face maps did not agree with each other, so this film cannot test the forecast.

NOT_RUN.text: The face-map test did not run: {reason}. It was set to run once, by rules written before any brain data was read.

scenes.title: How much is a forecast worth?

items.text: a forecast worth about {veq} real volunteers, and at least {veq_lo}
On a story chapter it never saw, TRIBE's forecast was worth about {veq} real volunteers, and at least {veq_lo}. It agreed with the classic sound test.
What it had to beat: word rate and the sound envelope.
LPP section 8, held out: recomputed with code built during the event; first measured Oct 22-23.

scored.text: Across {N} stories from public scans, TRIBE's forecast {wall_result}.

next_step.text: Too few stories passed the pre-registered data checks to score the wall; the rule says to report it as a next step.

not_run.text: Pre-registered, not run (GPU time ran out).

scenes.title: Intact story versus the same words scrambled

pass.text: Listeners' brains followed the intact story more than the scrambled one where TRIBE said they would ({k} of {N}, p = {p}).
What it had to beat: word rate and the sound envelope of each version.

fail.text: The intact-versus-scrambled test did not pass ({k} of {N}, p = {p}).
What it had to beat: word rate and the sound envelope of each version.

items.text: Every check's rule committed before its data was read. Nothing private leaves the laptop.

TRIBE v2 (Meta FAIR, CC BY-NC 4.0) was trained on CNeuroMod, BoldMoments, Lebel2023 and Wen2017 and tested by its authors on NNDb, LPP, Narratives and HCP (d'Ascoli et al. 2026, arXiv 2605.04326); Emo-FilM and the Blender films are new to it.
